title: NimbleHealth x Redwood - security & privacy review
next_steps: Redwood to confirm whether 'no content persisted' can be applied for Hosted API orgs
Customer to send their retention / logging requirements in writing
Schedule technical deep dive on observability redaction and audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-02-03
Time: 2:00pm ET
Duration: 47 min
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood), Dev Patel (Redwood), Priya Nair (NimbleHealth), Jon Feldman (NimbleHealth), Alicia Wu (NimbleHealth)

Summary (auto)
- Customer asked about data retention, logging, and whether Redwood stores prompts/responses.
- Discussed redaction in tracing and support workflows.
- Next steps: Redwood to confirm feasibility and document controls.

Transcript
[00:00] Alex Martinez: Cool, thanks everyone for making time. This is mostly a security and privacy walkthrough, and then we can do a quick recap at the end.
[00:24] Priya Nair: Yep. Our big items are retention and access. Specifically, we cant have patient content sitting in vendor logs.
[00:41] Dev Patel: Totally. When you say content, is that prompts and completions?
[00:46] Priya Nair: Exactly. Prompts and responses. Also any trace payloads.
[01:05] Jon Feldman: And like, were fine with request IDs and latency metrics, but not the bodies. We call it ephemeral processing internally.
[01:29] Alex Martinez: Got it. So operational metadata ok, no prompt/response persisted.
[01:44] Priya Nair: Right. And not just we delete after 30 days. We need it to never be stored at rest.
[02:07] Dev Patel: Okay. Redwood has observability and support tooling that can include payload sampling in some modes. For enterprise we can disable content capture and enforce redaction.
[02:32] Alicia Wu: Just to be clear, we would need that as a contractual requirement, not best effort.
[02:49] Alex Martinez: Understood. We can document the controls and put it into the security addendum.

[05:10] Jon Feldman: Where do logs actually go? Like CloudWatch, Datadog, whatever?
[05:18] Dev Patel: For Hosted, we ship metrics and traces through our pipeline; logs are centralized. For this requirement we would configure it so the payload fields are not logged.
[05:39] Priya Nair: Also, can support see our data?
[05:44] Alex Martinez: We use RBAC and a break-glass workflow, but for no content orgs we also restrict tooling so it cant display content.

[10:02] Priya Nair: Were comparing this to Bedrock and OpenAI. They both say they dont train on data, but we care more about retention.
[10:15] Alex Martinez: Makes sense. Our stance is: we dont train on customer data; and we can apply retention controls including no content logging for certain deployments.

[41:30] Alex Martinez: Recap: NimbleHealth requires zero retention of prompt/response content, including traces and debug logs; operational metadata ok. Well confirm implementation details and send language for the addendum.
[42:00] Priya Nair: Yep, thats the key requirement.
